Anya (Docs): Quick sync request 1: Drafting a compact docs style + naming PR focused on voice, canonical product names, and a tiny glossary. Need quick takes on: 1) tone, 2) exact product name forms, 3) ambiguous glossary terms (serving runtime, Dedicated vs Reserved vs Private).
Sam (Eng): Engineering-forward but approachable. Use examples that devs can copy/paste. For names: use full brand name on first mention (Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private) then short form after.
Kai (Product): Agrees with Sam. Tone: neutral, factual. Call out tradeoffs (latency vs cost) rather than marketing claims.
George (Research): For "serving runtime" glossary please include that it covers kernel selection and KV cache behavior and why that matters for latency/throughput. One short sentence is fine.
Anya (Docs): Proposed glossary blurb: `Serving runtime 014 The GPU-optimized inference engine that executes model requests, manages KV cache, and selects optimized kernels based on model/workload characteristics (see /eng-runtime).` Planning to add parenthetical about batching vs latency.
Emma (Docs): Also want a small SDK snippet guideline. Prefer using official SDK calls and consistent variable names. Example to include in PR: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }); await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Summarize the doc' });`
Sam (Eng): Small technical note: internal repos still use variations like "reserved capacity" or "dedicated pool". I can run a grep and paste matches in the PR for targeted edits.
Anya (Docs): Good — I'll include a migration checklist in the PR: - search/replace deprecated variants - update code examples to branded SDK API - fix internal links to eng runtime docs - add one-line tooltips for product pages.
Kai (Product): Add a one-liner for Private: `Redwood Private 014 customer-managed control plane for VPC or on-prem deployments.`
George (Research): Add a line to serving runtime entry: `(includes batching and KV caching behavior that trade off latency and throughput).`
Anya (Docs): Noted. Also planning to standardize shorthand mapping: API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize. Avoid generic terms like "reserved" unless quoting UX.
Emma (Docs): I'll do an editorial pass after PR opens. If marketing needs exact phrasing retained, flag it in comments so I don't auto-rewrite.
doc-bot: New PR opened by Anya (Docs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/425 1 "docs: style + naming glossary"
Sam (Eng): Pasted grep results in PR comments: 3 files use "reserved capacity", 2 use "dedicated pool". I'll follow up with proposed minimal diffs.
Anya (Docs): Thanks. Intent is surgical edits only, docs-only change, no content shifts. Tagging @Emma for copyedit and @Kai for product sign-off.
Emma (Docs): Will review tomorrow AM and flag any spots where phrasing would break existing exact-match tests.
Kai (Product): Looks good to me. Happy with the approach.
Anya (Docs): Great, closing this thread. I'll iterate in PR comments. Thanks all! :sparkles:
